uv and pip handle packages that exist on more than one index differently.
When a package exists on multiple indexes, uv checks indexes in order, preferring --extra-index-url indexes before the default index.
uv stops searching at the first index that contains the package and only considers candidate versions present in that index.

pip combines candidate versions from all indexes and selects the best version from the combined set, without guaranteeing search order and assuming packages are unique by name and version across indexes.
uv's default behavior is intended to protect against dependency confusion attacks, such as the torchtriton incident in December 2022.
If a package exists on an internal index, uv's default is to always install it from the internal index and never from PyPI.
The --index-strategy command-line option and UV_INDEX_STRATEGY environment variable became available as of v0.1.29.
The default value for index strategy is 'first-index', which limits candidate versions to the first index containing the package, checking --extra-index-url indexes before the default index.

uv can manage PyTorch projects and dependencies across Python versions and environments, including controlling for the choice of accelerator.
Running `uv add torch torchvision` installs CPU builds on Windows and macOS and CUDA-enabled builds on Linux.
You can add a PyTorch index to pyproject.toml and point torch and torchvision at it to get a specific variant across platforms.
Index options in the guide include CPU-only, CUDA 11.8, 12.6, 12.8, 13.0, ROCm 7.2, and Intel GPUs.
Setting `explicit = true` on the index ensures generic dependencies continue coming from PyPI.
Some features require uv version 0.4.3 or later.
